# A fold stays scalar when regrouping it would change the result or when the
# accumulator is used anywhere else in the loop: a float sum (addition is not
# associative), a running prefix, an operator that cannot be regrouped, a second
# fold into the same local, an accumulator that is also an operand, an
# accumulator that outlives the function, and an element type without a vector.

cp ops.go ops.go.orig
loopvec -split .
! stdout .
! stderr .
! exists ops_simd.go
cmp ops.go ops.go.orig

loopvec -json .
cmpenv stdout stdout.want

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

func FloatSum(a []float32) float32 {
	var s float32
	for i := range a {
		s += a[i]
	}
	return s
}

func FloatMax(a []float64) float64 {
	m := a[0]
	for i := range a {
		m = max(m, a[i])
	}
	return m
}

func Prefix(a, b []int32) {
	var s int32
	for i := range a {
		s += a[i]
		b[i] = s
	}
}

func Subtract(a []int32) int32 {
	var s int32
	for i := range a {
		s -= a[i]
	}
	return s
}

func TwoFolds(a, b []int32) int32 {
	var s int32
	for i := range a {
		s += a[i]
		s += b[i]
	}
	return s
}

func OwnOperand(a []int32) int32 {
	var s int32 = 1
	for i := range a {
		s += a[i] * s
	}
	return s
}

var total int32

func Global(a []int32) {
	for i := range a {
		total += a[i]
	}
}

func Plain(a []int) int {
	var s int
	for i := range a {
		s += a[i]
	}
	return s
}
